## Scoped partial result; broad question unresolved
A one-sided binary process has shifted laws converging weakly to the stationary mixture of constant paths, but under every coupling with that limit its coordinate mismatch probability tends to 1/2. Thus Thorisson Problem 3.3's illustrative synchronous metric-convergence proposal fails even in probability.

The broader request for some other two-process coupling characterization remains unresolved. This is not a counterexample to the distinct setwise-convergence problem 9900005. One substantive approach was used.

## Independent review
Separate adversarial review: PASS for the scoped synchronous counterexample, with unchanged proof SHA-256 `7123c345d3ecdf4fecb8941596687da54c44e169831eb23177ea485fa8386722`.
- 885 author assertions reproduced exactly
- 3,044 independent exact assertions pass
- Arbitrary-coupling, full-path conditioning, metric and dependent finite-offset arguments independently audited
- Review code, receipts and required frozen proof snapshot included

The review is independent AI review, not formal verification, external peer review or a novelty certificate.

## Source boundary
The complete relevant original section was recovered as indexed primary PDF text, but direct retrieval of the complete original PDF failed. Published-preview and Asmussen-source limitations are retained. Historical priority is unestablished. The ordinary Skorohod/Dudley family-of-copies theorem is not misrepresented as a single-path coupling.
